project_type: Single-file browser game — static HTML/CSS/JS, no build step, no server
build_system: None — open index.html directly in a browser. No npm, no bundler, no compile step. Both files (index.html, NODEBREAK.html) are standalone.
test_framework: None — verification is manual browser testing. Open the file, click 'Initialize Sequence', watch the full intro play.

verification_instructions: 1. Open index.html in Chrome (or Edge) via the browser's File menu or drag-drop. 2. Click 'Initialize Sequence'. 3. Watch and listen: scanner beam appears (~0.5s), flash+eyelids close/open (~3-3.5s), brain builds node-by-node (~4-10s), dialogue sequence plays through all 11 lines with matching audio. 4. After VAEL's final line the scene should fade to black and navigate to NODEBREAK.html. To verify audio fix: open DevTools Network tab, filter by Media, confirm all MP3 requests return 200 and each audio plays fully before the next line starts.
snapshot_or_generated_files: assets/*.mp3 — generated by generate_audio.py (pip install edge-tts then python generate_audio.py). Do NOT regenerate during this task — existing MP3s are correct. lab_background.jpg is a static asset.
environment_constraints: Windows filesystem paths with spaces (f:\Shreyash DOC\shreyash\Nodebreak\). Browser autoplay policy: AudioContext and new Audio() must be created inside or after a user gesture (the 'Initialize Sequence' button click). No external CDN links or libraries allowed. Everything must work by opening the file directly (file:// protocol).
contribution_requirements: No AGENTS.md or CONTRIBUTING.md exists. Key rule from task: Pure HTML/CSS/JS only — no external libraries, no CDN links, no frameworks. Preserve the sci-fi/AI-awakening/cyberpunk aesthetic. Do not break the narrative flow. Keep all existing assets working.
key_patterns: All JS lives in a single <script> block at the bottom of index.html. CSS is all in one <style> block in <head>. Sequence flow: startBtn click → playCinematicIntro() → spawns brain nodes → setTimeout(showNextDialogue, 1000) → showNextDialogue() iterates through vnSequence[] array using logIndex counter → each entry has {speaker, image, text, audio?, alert?, awaken?}. Audio via new Audio(path).play(). Canvas animation via requestAnimationFrame(drawBrain) self-loop. isAwake and colorProgress globals drive the blue-to-red color transition. No module system, no classes — all globals and functions at script scope.
